objective: Reconcile a third fresh scheduler-health timing window across nominal live schedule, durable worker produced/started/completed timestamps, Git persistence timestamps, and scheduler last_run_time to determine which clocks are safe for queue-delay inference and whether any evidence-based narrow phase fix is now justified.
finding_summary: Evidence Analyst R51 durable produced_at was 04:00:22 JST, its Git persistence commit was 04:18:05 JST, and scheduler last_run_time was about 04:20:25 JST; these clocks are not interchangeable worker-start or queue timestamps.
MAIN R51 durable lease started at 04:18:00 JST for nominal :15 and completed at 04:20:00 JST, giving an exact durable start offset of about +3 minutes and about 2 minutes runtime.

At the live scheduler snapshot, MAIN scheduler last_run_time still represented the prior cycle despite the R51 durable lease already being completed, proving scheduler last_run_time can lag authoritative worker state.
Runtime overlap across adjacent five-minute phases remains real, but three recent windows do not establish monotonic queue-delay accumulation or a deterministic exact-time collision.
A scheduler phase auto-fix remains underdetermined; authoritative due_at/queued_at/started_at/finished_at telemetry is needed before attributing coarse offsets to queue delay.

trigger_source.prior_recommendation: Collect exact due/queued/started/finished telemetry across at least three comparable windows before scheduler timing mutation.
trigger_source.control_scheduler_health: CTRL-20260922T025652+0900-R28-9A9BFB1F reports YELLOW persistent-delay signal and no deterministic exact collision.

follow_up_recommendation: Do not repeat coarse scheduler last_run_time sampling as if it were queue telemetry. Prefer authoritative scheduler-side nominal_due_at/queued_at/started_at/finished_at data, or durable worker lease started_at/completed_at where available, before any phase mutation.
